subject: Renewal + mid-contract top-up: capacity escrow and smoothing options
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cardiffai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@cardiffai.com>, procurement@cardiffai.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal + top-up guidance—CardiffAI

Hi Monica,

We’re approaching our Oct 1 renewal and we expect a 35–40% increase in inference volume across two product lines after the new recommendation model ships. Procurement asked for a renewal quote that can:
- Add a mid-contract top-up (one-off capacity increase) that is co-termed with the existing contract,
- Smooth billing so the impact is not front-loaded on the first invoice, and
- Include a short-term surge buffer for Q4 launch traffic spikes.

Could you share options and pricing for:
1) Annualize the new commitment vs. adding a one-off top-up bucket (with proration).
2) A smoothing invoice schedule (quarterly amortization or monthly installments).
3) Any temporary surge credits or capped overage rate for the first 90 days.

We’re on a constrained procurement timeline—would appreciate a options matrix and recommended path by EOD Tuesday (Aug 31).

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Ops, CardiffAI

Attachments: Procurement_SOW_v2.pdf (reference)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cardiffai.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + top-up guidance—CardiffAI

Thanks Elaine — wrote up three options and looping in our pricing lead to get exact numbers. High level:

Option A — Annualize & pro-rate (recommended for predictable unit economics)
- We fold the expected uplift into the renewal amount and annualize over the 12‑month term.
- Billing: one adjusted renewal invoice (prorated for any partial period) plus monthly usage reconciliation.
- Discount: modest volume discount tied to committed annual tokens; deeper at +50% uplift.

Option B — One-off co-term top-up bucket (fast to implement)
- Add a top-up bucket that is co‑termed to your renewal date. Top-up is billed pro‑rata for remainder of the term.
- Billing: top-up invoice up front, then normal renewal on term date.
- Discount: smaller uplift discount but lower commitment.

Option C — Smoothing + surge guard (operational simplicity)
- Split the uplift cost across N invoices (quarterly or monthly) and include a 90‑day surge buffer at a capped overage rate.
- Example: 50% of uplift amortized over next 3 invoices; surge buffer 10% of uplift at capped price.

I’ll attach an Excel scenario matrix with modeled invoices and effective unit prices. Ben, Naomi & Rishi — can you review the attached scenarios and flag which one gives procurement the clearest path from a billing/finance perspective?

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: Cardiff_Renewal_TopUp_Scenarios.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + top-up guidance—CardiffAI

Quick thoughts after scanning the scenarios:

- Finance preference: they’ll want predictable ARR and minimal manual true-ups. Option A (annualize) is easiest for forecasting but requires higher commitment visibility from Cardiff.
- Procurement preference: Option B is attractive because it preserves flexibility. If we do B, recommend adding a small voucher/credit for surge (2–4% of uplift) to offset invoice sticker shock.
- Cash/PS trade: if Cardiff agrees to a 9‑12 month annualize path we can offer a 6% blended uplift discount and an extra 30k GPU-credit voucher to use within first 60 days post-launch.

Action items for proposal:
1) Produce two formal quotes (A and B) with exact numbers and amortization schedules.
2) For Option C, create a clearly labeled surge cap and an example invoice to show smoothing effect.

I’ve updated the Excel with finance-level notes. Naomi — can you confirm the maximum discount window we can approve without legal sign-off? Rishi — any contractual constraints on co-term top-ups we should call out?

-Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cardiffai.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@cardiffai.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + top-up guidance—CardiffAI

Thanks for the quick turnaround, team. Elaine — attached are two formalized quote attachments:

- Quote 1 (Annualize — recommended): folds projected 40% uplift into the annual commitment; shows effective per‑token pricing, monthly amortization example, and a 6% blended discount. Includes a 30k GPU‑credit voucher usable in first 60 days.
- Quote 2 (Co‑term Top‑up): a co‑term top‑up bucket for the remainder of your upcoming term; pro‑rata billing example included, plus a 3% purchase credit for surge (applied as a billing credit if overages exceed the buffer).

Key callouts:
- Smoothing: we can amortize uplift over 3 invoices (quarterly) or 12 invoices (monthly) — you pick cadence.
- Surge guard: 90‑day capped overage rate at 20% above standard unit price for any usage beyond the buffer.
- Implementation: co‑term top‑ups are operationally simple and can be live within 5 business days; annualize changes require a signed amendment and a reissue of the renewal invoice.

Please see the attached spreadsheet with side‑by‑side cashflow tables. If procurement wants we can prepare a one‑page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lists milestones and invoicing checkpoints (I’ll draft it).

Next step: can we schedule a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the two quotes and the example invoices? Available windows: 09:00–10:30 or 14:00–15:30 BST.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Cardiff_Renewal_TopUp_Scenarios.xlsx, Redwood_Uplift_Terms_v3.pdf

From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@cardiffai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@cardiffai.com>
Cc: procurement@cardiffai.com
Date: 2026-09-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + top-up guidance—CardiffAI

Monica, Elaine — thanks for the options, that spreadsheet made it easy to compare. Procurement prefers Option B (co‑term top‑up) but with a 6‑month amortization window rather than upfront billing — they want to avoid a large CAPEX hit this quarter. Two clarifying asks before we sign:

1) Can you convert the top‑up invoice into three equal installments over 6 months (so amortized monthly but invoiced as three milestones)?
2) For the surge guard, can the capped overage rate be fixed in the SOW rather than an ad‑hoc billing credit? Procurement wants a contractual cap.

If those are ok, we’ll route for signature next week. Appreciate the GPU voucher offer — that helps the launch budget.

Regards,
Tom Hsu
VP Product, CardiffAI
